text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ninety percent of Turks who called or sent faxes to the paper favour publishing the name of an anonymous doctor who sexually abused his patients.
- The Netherlands, France and Britain send optimistic signals to Turkey on its claim to be included on the list of countries for European Union (EU) full membership.
- More than 200 Turks have been successfully evacuated from Albania by the Turkish navy.
- The report on a security scandal is finally given to parliamentary commission investigating the affair.
- A U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) report outlines Turkey's role as a bridge in internatioanl drug trafficking.
- Foreign investors await Council of State's decision on a natural gas plant to be build in western city of Izmir.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says he is open to any alternative government formula as long as it does not involve Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party.
